title: Scheme atlas of a sheaf pullback and its test schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with sheaves of sets on its big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $F,G,H$ be sheaves with maps $f:F\to H$ and $g:G\to H$. Suppose $\Delta_H$ is representable by schemes, and let $a:h_U\to F$ and $b:h_V\to G$ be representable surjective etale maps from $S$-schemes $U,V$, with these scheme-test properties understood as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Put $P(T)=\{(x,y):f(x)=g(y)\}\subseteq F(T)\times G(T)$ and $W=h_U\times_Hh_V$, with their pointwise presheaf fibre products. Then $W$ is represented by the scheme obtained by pulling back $\Delta_H$ along $h_{U\times_SV}\to H\times H$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The induced natural transformation $w:W\to P$ is representable surjective etale. More precisely, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and natural transformation $t:h_T\to P$, with components $x:h_T\to F$ and $y:h_T\to G$, let $A$ and $B$ represent $h_T\times_Fh_U$ and $h_T\times_Gh_V$. There is a canonical isomorphism $h_T\times_PW\cong h_{A\times_TB}$ over $h_T$, taking a pair of lifts to the corresponding compatible $U,V$ sections. Its scheme projection is the composite $A\times_TB\to B\to T$, and both arrows are surjective etale.

source.place: Tag 04T9 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces-over-sheaf-with-representable-diagonal), last paragraph: construction and scheme tests of the atlas.

proof.text: Test the representable diagonal of H on the product U ×_S V. Yoneda preserves this binary product. For its product cone, the presheaf pullback W of a≫f and b≫g is the pullback of the diagonal: construct the lift into W from the two projections of a competing cone; the diagonal equation makes their H-images equal. Product and pullback uniqueness prove the universal property. Uniqueness of these two diagonal pullback squares gives h_D ≅ W. Its projection to h_(U×_S V) gives both required Yoneda component equations. This is the private helper diagonal_square and the first part of fibreProduct_atlas_tests.

source.place: Tag 04T9, lemma-fibre-product-spaces-over-sheaf-with-representable-diagonal, last paragraph; expanded scheme-test calculation.

proof.text: For any chosen representing square of a scheme test of a (and likewise b), compare it with the witness supplied by IsEtale or IsSurjective. Pullback uniqueness gives an isomorphism of the representing presheaves; Yoneda full faithfulness gives an isomorphism of schemes over T. Since étaleness and surjectivity respect isomorphisms, the properties hold for the projection in every chosen representing square. This is property_of_test. In particular the given α and β are étale and surjective.

source.place: Tag 04T9, lemma-fibre-product-spaces-over-sheaf-with-representable-diagonal, last paragraph; expanded scheme-test calculation.

proof.text: For the given t and representing squares h_A,h_B, map h_(A×_T B) to W by its two projections followed by qA and qB. The square with t and w commutes by the representing-square equations. Given a competing pullback cone, its U and V components and its T component lift uniquely through h_A and h_B. Their T components agree, so Yoneda preservation of the scheme pullback lifts them to h_(A×_T B). The projection equations and uniqueness follow componentwise from the three pullback universal properties. This constructs the pullback square in test_square. Its canonical isomorphism to the chosen presheaf pullback gives exactly the three asserted equations.

source.place: Tag 04T9, lemma-fibre-product-spaces-over-sheaf-with-representable-diagonal, last paragraph; expanded scheme-test calculation.

proof.text: Apply the singleton base-change results to α along β. The forgetful functor Over S → Scheme preserves this pullback. Since α is étale and surjective, its base change pr_B:A×_T B→B has both properties. Lean uses MorphismProperty.of_isPullback with the Mathlib étale and surjective stability instances, the singleton specialization of the cited covering lemma.

source.place: Tag 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale, and Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective; singleton case.

proof.text: For any scheme test t, choose étale representing squares for a and b and apply the comparison just proved. It gives an actual representing square for w with projection pr_B≫β. The singleton composition results say this scheme map is étale and surjective. Project the conjunction of properties to obtain IsRepresentable, IsEtale and IsSurjective separately. Lean uses the Mathlib composition instances, the singleton specialization of the cited covering lemma.

source.place: Tag 0217, lemma-etale, part (2), singleton case; scheme-test definition in spaces.tex.

Step 5: the etale-covering base-change leaf for the singleton {alpha} along beta. Step 6: the composition leaf, giving exactly the scheme-test definition. lean.statement: theorem fibreProduct_atlas_tests {S : Scheme.{u}} (F G H : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (f : F.obj ⟶ H.obj) (g : G.obj ⟶ H.obj) (hH : IsRepresentable (prod.lift (𝟙 H.obj) (𝟙 H.obj))) (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ G.obj) (hae : IsEtale a) (has : IsSurjective a) (hbe : IsEtale b) (hbs : IsSurjective b) : (∃ (D : Over S) (e : yoneda.obj D ≅ Limits.pullback (a ≫ f) (b ≫ g)) (p : D ⟶ prod U V), e.hom ≫ Limits.pullback.fst (a ≫ f) (b ≫ g) = yoneda.map (p ≫ prod.fst) ∧ e.hom ≫ Limits.pullback.snd (a ≫ f) (b ≫ g) = yoneda.map (p ≫ prod.snd) ∧ IsPullback (e.hom ≫ Limits.pullback.fst (a ≫ f) (b ≫ g) ≫ a ≫ f) (yoneda.map p) (prod.lift (𝟙 H.obj) (𝟙 H.obj)) (prod.lift (yoneda.map (prod.fst : prod U V ⟶ U) ≫ a ≫ f) (yoneda.map (prod.snd : prod U V ⟶ V) ≫ b ≫ g))) ∧ IsRepresentable (fibreProductAtlasMap f g a b) ∧ IsEtale (fibreProductAtlasMap f g a b) ∧ IsSurjective (fibreProductAtlasMap f g a b) ∧ ∀ (T : Over S) (t : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Limits.pullback f g) (A B : Over S) (α : A ⟶ T) (β : B ⟶ T) (qA : yoneda.obj A ⟶ yoneda.obj U) (qB : yoneda.obj B ⟶ yoneda.obj V), IsPullback qA (yoneda.map α) a (t ≫ Limits.pullback.fst f g) → IsPullback qB (yoneda.map β) b (t ≫ Limits.pullback.snd f g) → ∃ e : yoneda.obj (Limits.pullback α β) ≅ Limits.pullback t (fibreProductAtlasMap f g a b), e.hom ≫ Limits.pullback.fst t (fibreProductAtlasMap f g a b) = yoneda.map (Limits.pullback.snd α β ≫ β) ∧ e.hom ≫ Limits.pullback.snd t (fibreProductAtlasMap f g a b) ≫ Limits.pullback.fst (a ≫ f) (b ≫ g) = yoneda.map (Limits.pullback.fst α β) ≫ qA ∧ e.hom ≫ Limits.pullback.snd t (fibreProductAtlasMap f g a b) ≫ Limits.pullback.snd (a ≫ f) (b ≫ g) = yoneda.map (Limits.pullback.snd α β) ≫ qB ∧ Etale (Limits.pullback.snd α β).left ∧ Surjective (Limits.pullback.snd α β).left ∧ Etale β.left ∧ Surjective β.left
